title: Object-Relational Mapping and Database Testing
subtopics: Active Record as an ecosystem option
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of object-relational mapping and database testing in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply object-relational mapping and database testing in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to database test isolation and cleanup and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Object-Relational Mapping and Database Testing through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding object-relational mapping and database testing helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Object-Relational Mapping and Database Testing helps you reason about orm concepts. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: ORM concepts. Then connect it to Active Record as an ecosystem option. The remaining syllabus points—Mapping records to objects, Database test isolation and cleanup—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Example: Object-Relational Mapping and Database Testing
content_blocks.code:
require "sqlite3"
db = SQLite3::Database.new(":memory:")
db.execute("CREATE TABLE tasks (id INTEGER, title TEXT)")
db.execute("INSERT INTO tasks VALUES (?, ?)", [1, "Learn Ruby"])
puts db.get_first_value("SELECT title FROM tasks WHERE id = ?", 1)
db.close
